related_synthesis_entries.claim: The close-pair logarithmic derivative has a dominant winding-one component; uniform control of the background preserves a unique local root, and contour selection makes that root analytic, justifying its even power-series expansion.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: Uniformity requires gap height strictly below one over pi and sufficiently large degree; it does not establish a global matching of every gap to a derivative root.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The decisive object is the image D of a boundary contour under the logarithmic derivative, compared with a model image E of index one. Decomposing f'/f into the nearby-zero term and a background sum turns all remaining zeros into a perturbation; half-plane localization preserves the winding when that background stays below the dominant term.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The small upper and lower boundary arcs map near large half-circles, while the other two arcs must remain in opposite half-planes. For the difficult arc, -g is positive and Lemma 8.2 maximizes the real part of 1/(z-ζ) over |ζ|=1. Lemma 8.3 then bounds each remaining-zero contribution by [πθ0/N+O(θ0²/N²)](-g); after summation the positivity factor tends to 1-πθ0, so it is positive uniformly for |θ0|≤T<1/π once N≥N(T).
directed.conceptual_reading: Root uniqueness is reduced to stability of a winding number rather than direct solution of f'=0. The strict limiting margin 1-πθ0 explains both the gap threshold and why sufficiently large degree is required.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The logarithmic derivative bridges zeros to a planar image curve whose half-plane placement controls its index. Lemma 8.2 compresses the unknown locations of all other unit-circle zeros into a sharp scalar extremum, and elementary tangent/secant remainder bounds make the resulting perturbation uniform.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The estimate is uniform only below the strict threshold T<1/π and for N≥N(T); the contour radius may depend on the parameter configuration. It proves a local derivative-root count in the chosen disk, not a global matching of all gaps to derivative roots.
directed.uncertainty: The extraction corrupts epsilon symbols and fragments some interval and inequality displays, especially around the arc-neighborhood estimate. The winding mechanism and limiting margin are legible, but exact constants and endpoints should be checked against the scan.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Once the derivative root is unique, the contour integral turns that implicitly defined root into an analytic selector. A contour can be fixed uniformly on each compact parameter subset, so joint analyticity of f and residue extraction give analytic dependence without solving for the root explicitly.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For the already established unique root z₀=ς(Θ₀) of f', equation (8.19) represents ς(Θ₀) by (1/(2πi)) times the contour integral of z f''(Θ₀;z)/f'(Θ₀;z). The contour radius can be chosen so this integral selects the same unique root for every Θ₀ in any prescribed compact subset of the interior of P_N^(T); joint analyticity then yields analyticity throughout that interior.
directed.conceptual_reading: Uniqueness is converted into regular parameter dependence by replacing pointwise root choice with a residue-defined local coordinate. Compact-local choices suffice because analyticity is a local property and the selected root agrees on overlaps.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge object is the logarithmic-derivative contour integral for f': it converts an isolated zero into a holomorphic function of the configuration parameters. This avoids making an explicit branch choice for the moving root.
directed.boundary_or_failure: No single contour is claimed to work over the whole parameter domain; it is chosen uniformly only on a desired compact interior subset. The conclusion depends on the preceding uniqueness result and does not address boundary parameters or a global correspondence between gaps and derivative roots.
directed.uncertainty: The semantic role of (8.19) is clear, but the extracted display has awkward ordering; its exact numerator and normalization should be scan-verified as the assignment notes.
